originals.why: Natural North Welsh. 'dal i chwarae' means keep playing, which uses chwarae in the sense taught here.
Natural North Welsh. 'cytuno i chwarae' means agreed to play, the same sense as taught.
Natural North Welsh. 'wedi mynd i chwarae' means has gone to play, the same sense as taught.

topups.ko: 너 그녀가 이번에는 경기할 수 있다고 생각해?
topups.why: The Korean needed a question mark because the Welsh is a question. It closely mirrors the seed.
The Welsh and Korean are both fine, but 5 USE rows are already kept.
'chwarae efo dy ffrind' means playing with a friend for fun, so 경기하다 (playing a match) is the wrong sense. The Korean also lacked a question mark.
